title: timeboxed-review-handoff-scratch-riley
body:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for running timeboxed review sessions and creating a lightweight handoff template for larger PRs. Goal: reduce reviewer cognitive load, make followups actionable, and make it easy to resume a paused review after interruptions.

Why timebox reviews?
- Limits context fatigue (15-30m windows).
- Forces prioritization: surface the biggest risks first.
- Makes reviews predictable for both author and reviewer.

Session formats (pick one based on patch size):
1) Micro (<= 10 files, simple): 15 minutes. Focus: correctness, test gaps, risky lines.
2) Medium (10-40 files, internal API changes): 30 minutes. Focus: API contract, migrations, perf impact, tests.
3) Deep (>40 files or infra changes): 60 minutes + pairing. Focus: safety, rollout plan, monitoring signals.

Pre-review checklist (author) — paste at top of PR description:
- TL;DR (1-2 lines): what changed and why.
- Scope summary: files touched + high-level areas.
- Risk level: low/medium/high + short rationale.
- Rollout plan: feature flag? canary? immediate revert path?
- Tests: unit/integration/e2e coverage and quick instructions to run locally.
- Perf impact: rough numbers (locally measured) or N/A.
- Data migrations / DB changes: runbook + rollback notes.
- Related tickets / design docs (links).

Reviewer quick checklist: (use as running notes in PR comment)
- [ ] Build passes locally / CI stable? note failures.
- [ ] Does the change preserve invariants? list quick invariants checked.
- [ ] Edge cases: list 2–3 obvious edge cases and whether handled.
- [ ] Tests: are they meaningful and brittle? suggest one explicit test if missing.
- [ ] Observability: any metrics/logs to add? note specific metrics.
- [ ] Backwards compatibility: mention API/DB compat concerns.
- [ ] Perf/regression risk: flag hotspots and suggest perf smoke test.
- [ ] Security/privacy: any PII or auth changes? escalate if unsure.

How to run a 30-minute session (template):
- 0–3m: read PR TL;DR, author notes, hit high-level file list.
- 3–12m: scan diff for obvious correctness and API surface. Write inline comments for small nits.
- 12–20m: identify up to 3 substantive risks (security, perf, data). Ask targeted questions.
- 20–25m: propose concrete next actions (tests to add, refactors, monitoring).
- 25–30m: summary comment: accept with X small nits / request Y changes / suggest pairing for deep items.

Handoff template (copy into PR description under "Handoff"):
- Ready for handoff to: @who (name + timezone)
- Why this needs human handoff: (e.g., DB migration, infra change, rollout coordination)
- Expected rollout date / window
- Steps to validate post-deploy (3 quick checks)
- Revert plan (exact commands or link to runbook)
- Communication recipients (pager/Slack channel, on-call)

Quick revert safety mini-plan (for all medium+ PRs):
- Keep a one-line revert command in PR (git revert <sha> && push).
- Smoke-check endpoint(s) and expected status codes.
- Tag owner for rollback: @oncall-team or person.

Examples / micro-templates for inline comments:
- If you find a missing test: "Test idea: add unit test asserting X for input Y (fast to run)."
- If API contract unclear: "Clarify: does caller ever pass null here? If yes, should we validate?"
- For perf risk: "This loop runs per-request; can we memoize or early-return? Quick benchmark?"

Signals that should bump priority to pairing / deep review:
- DB migrations altering production rows (even if small).
- Security surface changes (auth, token handling).
- Large refactors touching many modules with subtle invariants.
- New infra (k8s manifests, helm charts) or network config changes.

Open questions / annoyances I keep running into (notes for future tweaks):
- CI flakes: we need an easier flag to skip long e2e for micro changes so reviewers can focus on logic.
- PR descriptions still too long hallucination-style; encourage strict TL;DR + bullet lists.
- Linter noise: sometimes hides real diffs; maybe a pre-commit grouping for style-only commits.

Small experiments to try next sprint (hypotheses):
- 15-minute morning/afternoon review windows where volunteers are available to do triage; measure PR turnaround.
- Auto-checklist bot that ensures author pasted pre-review checklist; fail CI if missing.
- Small "review buddy" rota for deep changes (pairing slots scheduled weekly).

Next actions (me):
- Prototype a short checklist template and paste into the PR template file. (GH-refs: repo/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md)
- Try one 30m pairing session with @Amir next Wed for the big infra PR.
- Draft a tiny bot message template to remind authors to include the handoff block when DB migrations are present.

Scratch notes (stream-of-consciousness):
- Keep comments succinct. Avoid long threads that turn into debates. Use threads only to resolve a technical blocker.
- For low-risk refactors, prefer merging sooner with a follow-up cleanup PR than a long bike-shed review.
- Consider adding a single line in PR title: "review: quick / medium / deep" to set expectations.

-- end of scratchpad --
